scenario.summary: A threat actor used SEO poisoning on Bing to deliver trojanized IT management installers, leading to Bumblebee and AdaptixC2 infections. The intrusion escalated to a full network compromise where the actor performed credential dumping, established persistent remote access via RustDesk, exfiltrated data, and ultimately deployed Akira ransomware.

meta.rationale: The hunt begins by identifying IT administrators and systems where management tools are already installed, as these are the primary targets for SEO poisoning lures like 'ManageEngine'. If no specific hosts are provided, it runs fleet-wide with a focus on user-writable directories.
meta.hypothesis: An attacker has compromised an IT administrator via SEO poisoning, leading to the execution of a trojanized installer that side-loads Bumblebee and establishes AdaptixC2 connectivity.

hunt.name: Bumblebee Initial Access and C2 Deployment
hunt.description: This hunt identifies the initial entry point and command-and-control establishment of the Bumblebee malware. We start by scoping hosts with IT management tools typically targeted in SEO poisoning campaigns, then look for the specific MSI installers used as lures. The hunt pivots to detect the sideloading of msimg32.dll into legitimate system processes like consent.exe and corroborates this with network connections to known C2 infrastructure and DGA-patterned DNS lookups. An agent triages the multiple evidence streams to identify active infections before they move to lateral movement.

nodes.label: Scope hosts with targeted IT tools

config.content: SELECT DISTINCT device_hostname FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE instr(LOWER(package_name), 'manageengine') > 0 OR instr(LOWER(package_name), 'opmanager') > 0
config.description: Identify hosts that have IT management tools installed, as these users are likely the primary targets for SEO poisoning campaigns targeting admins.
config.expected_signal: A list of hostnames belonging to IT staff. If empty, the hunt continues unscoped.

primitive_config.label: Scope hosts with targeted IT tools
primitive_config.content: SELECT DISTINCT device_hostname FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE instr(LOWER(package_name), 'manageengine') > 0 OR instr(LOWER(package_name), 'opmanager') > 0
primitive_config.expected: A list of hostnames belonging to IT staff. If empty, the hunt continues unscoped.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, file_name, file_path, actor_user_name, time FROM hb_file_activity WHERE (instr(',' || '{{lure_msi_filenames}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(file_name) || ',') > 0 OR (LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\\users\\%' AND LOWER(file_name) LIKE '%.msi')) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Detect the download or presence of trojanized installers identified in the report, or any MSI in user-writable paths.
config.expected_signal: MSI file interaction in user profile folders like Downloads or Desktop. This provides the primary entry lead.

primitive_config.label: MSI activity in user directories
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, file_name, file_path, actor_user_name, time FROM hb_file_activity WHERE (instr(',' || '{{lure_msi_filenames}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(file_name) || ',') > 0 OR (LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\\users\\%' AND LOWER(file_name) LIKE '%.msi')) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: MSI file interaction in user profile folders like Downloads or Desktop. This provides the primary entry lead.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, module_path, time FROM hb_module_activity WHERE LOWER(module_name) = 'msimg32.dll' AND module_path IS NOT NULL AND LOWER(module_path) NOT LIKE 'c:\\windows\\system32\\%' AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Detect the side-loading of msimg32.dll from non-system directories, a core behavioral indicator for Bumblebee execution.
config.expected_signal: A module load for msimg32.dll where the path is within a user directory or C:\ProgramData. This is the primary behavioral detection candidate.

primitive_config.label: Bumblebee DLL side-loading
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, module_path, time FROM hb_module_activity WHERE LOWER(module_name) = 'msimg32.dll' AND module_path IS NOT NULL AND LOWER(module_path) NOT LIKE 'c:\\windows\\system32\\%' AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: A module load for msimg32.dll where the path is within a user directory or C:\ProgramData. This is the primary behavioral detection candidate.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, dst_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_port, time FROM hb_network_connection WHERE instr(',' || '{{c2_ips}}' || ',', ',' || dst_endpoint_ip || ',') > 0 AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify connections to the Adaptix and Bumblebee IPs associated with this campaign.
config.expected_signal: Network connections to known-bad infrastructure from hosts that also showed suspicious MSI or DLL activity.

primitive_config.label: Outbound traffic to C2 IPs
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, dst_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_port, time FROM hb_network_connection WHERE instr(',' || '{{c2_ips}}' || ',', ',' || dst_endpoint_ip || ',') > 0 AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')

config.content: SELECT query_hostname, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS hosts, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE LOWER(query_hostname) LIKE '%.org' AND length(replace(LOWER(query_hostname), '.org', '')) BETWEEN 8 AND 14 AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY query_hostname HAVING hosts <= 3 ORDER BY hosts ASC
config.description: Search for randomized .org domains matching the 8-14 character Bumblebee DGA pattern and filter for fleet rarity.
config.expected_signal: One or two randomized domains found on only one host. These represent the DGA signals that survive IP rotation.

config.objective: Determine if a host has been compromised via the reported SEO poisoning campaign. Weigh the presence of lure MSI files against the side-loading of msimg32.dll and communication with the listed infrastructure.
config.description: Consolidate results from the MSI leads, module loading, and network/DNS activity to confirm the initial access sequence.
config.expected_signal: A per-host verdict citing the combination of MSI files, non-standard DLL loads, and C2 traffic.
config.success_criteria: A per-host verdict of malicious | suspicious | benign, citing specific evidence rows.

config.question: The triage verdict is malicious for any host where side-loading or known C2 traffic was confirmed.
config.condition: The triage verdict is malicious for any host where side-loading or known C2 traffic was confirmed.
config.description: Determine the next action based on the agent's findings.
Contain the Bumblebee infection immediately to prevent AdaptixC2 lateral movement.
config.instructions: Isolate the identified endpoint. Revoke all active cloud and SSO sessions for the user account identified in the activity.

config.description: Conduct manual analysis to confirm the findings and look for signs of follow-on activity like AdaptixC2 beacons.
config.instructions: Review the host's C:\ProgramData and user profile directories for recently created .exe files with random names (potential AdaptixC2). Verify if consent.exe spawned any unusual child processes.

config.description: Finalize documentation and note any legitimate IT software that should be excluded from future runs.
